release_decision: No runtime default changed. #3882 is exact on prompt, continuation, and logit hashes in the Q35 2048/128 protocol, but prefill is effectively flat/slightly adverse and decode has material within-arm spread on a non-quiet host, so there is no model-speed claim. #3842 changes target numerics and remains on the multi-prompt quality, state, memory, and long-generation gate. #4048 is order/host-confounded, packed GDN failed its decode gate, the one-prompt DDTree probe does not justify a Qwen35 default, #3838 is closed unmerged, and #4171 remains conditional. ParoQuant, the tested pre-#3934 Majentik NVFP4 artifact, OptiQ, and DWQ showed no speed promotion in the fixed-token/forward-count measurements; historical NLL is not cross-artifact quality evidence; corrected NVFP4 remains untested and additionally requires the #3912 dimension guard. The FusionML result is a contended-host adverse observation, not a clean mechanism NO-GO. The next exact A/B queue is traced high-concurrency #4023 with #3922/#4009 production correctness, thermally controlled #1559 prefill, traced local Laguna work for #3843, sparse complete-state checkpoint simulation, and #1547 session-concurrency validation. Domino versus DFlash is the highest-priority Qwen27 drafter test; Bole reopens hybrid-tree feasibility as a separate Metal co-design. Rotated asymmetric KV is the best published smart-compression experiment for outlier-heavy Qwen, but needs local coding and long-context gates. MAPS-MLX is a falsifiable interaction experiment, not a measured speedup or release candidate.
